commitResults.messageBody: Tasks were previously only saved in memory and lost when user exits program. This commit adds serialization and deserialization using JSONL format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add typed date and time support
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines and events currently store temporal values as arbitrary strings, which prevents validation, formatting, and date-based queries.
This commit adds the record TaskDate to represent a serialisable Date and Time for our app.

commitResults.messageBody: Users cannot search the task list without manually inspecting every task.\n\nAdd a case-insensitive substring search over task descriptions and display the matching tasks. commitResults.messageBody: The project previously required a manual javac source-file list for compilation. This commit adds the Gradle wrapper, Java 25 configuration, JUnit support, executable JAR packaging, and Gradle-based UI test compilation.
The application had no automated tests for date parsing or task search behavior. This commit adds coverage for valid and invalid TaskDate values and case-insensitive ordered TaskList searches.
Integrate Gradle CheckStyle checks for production and test sources, using a project-local ruleset that matches the existing Java conventions.
Add a JavaFX entry point and command-driven task window while preserving the existing CLI and shared command, storage, and task logic.
Keep standard-library imports consistently ordered according to the project code style guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for task list invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList assumes that callers provide valid tasks, keywords, and indexes.

Assertions make these assumptions explicit during development while
preserving the existing exception behavior when assertions are disabled.

MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand duplicate the task update and
confirmation flow.

Centralizing that flow in Command keeps both commands consistent and
rejects unsupported update command types explicitly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams when loading stored tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage loads every non-blank line from the task file and converts it
into a task or corrupted-task record.

Use a stream pipeline for filtering, parsing, and collecting those
records while preserving their order and existing malformed-record
handling.

Users cannot reverse task changes after issuing a command, which makes
correcting accidental additions, deletions, and completion changes
inconvenient.

Add a session undo history and an undo command for task-list mutations.
Store inverse actions so task order and previous completion states are
restored without changing the persistent storage format.

Keep undo history in memory because it is scoped to one application session,
and restore a failed undo when saving the restored state is unsuccessful.
